newsitem.title: USA: Ramtron, Racom, Intag in FRAM pact.
newsitem.headline: Ramtron, Racom, Intag in FRAM pact.

text.p: Ramtron International Corp, Racom Systems Inc and Intag International Ltd said on Friday they entered into an agreement to boost the availability of Ramtron's ferroelectric random access memory (FRAM) technology for radio frequency identification markets.

The agreement is intended to increase the potential of selling FRAM-based smart cards and other radio frequency identification (RF/ID) applications in such markets as mass transit, automatic identification and industrial automation, the companies said.
RF/ID uses radio waves to power and transfer data between electronic tags or cards and a reader attached to a host computer system.
The companies said FRAM memory's high speed, low power and non-volatile characteristics simplify the design and maximize performance and reliability in RF/ID applications.
Ramtron, of Colorado Springs, developed the FRAM technology. Racom, of Greenwood Village, Colo., makes contactless smart-card systems. Intag, of Sydney, Australia, makes data-capture technologies.
